$comment: FLIPKART worker TEMPLATE. Do not edit this file — copy it:
and fill `proxies` there. The .local.json copy is gitignored because the
proxy URLs carry credentials, and the worker reads only that copy
(deploy/docker-compose.flipkart.yml). It refuses to start if it is missing.
This file sizes the worker: its proxies, identity pool and request budget.
HOW MANY Flipkart products are scraped, and HOW OFTEN, are set on the
dashboard under Settings -> Flipkart, where the API and both workers can
Sizing: Amazon's addresses sustain ~3.5 req/min each; assume the same per
proxy until measured. requests/min = products / interval x ~1.1, so
Watch the Flipkart scraper panel for blocks before raising anything.

connection.$comment: Proxies, not a household line: several addresses, no home-device warning.

$comment_proxies: Full URLs, one per proxy, credentials included: ["http://user:pass@1.2.3.4:8080", "http://user:pass@5.6.7.8:8080"]. Identities are spread across them evenly and stay on the same proxy for life. Empty means the worker sends from the host's own address, which Flipkart refuses on AWS.

identities.$comment: About 12 per proxy, matching the Amazon worker's density: with 3 proxies set count to 36. New identities fill the least-loaded proxy first.

ipCap.$comment: PER PROXY. Starts at 3 requests/min and learns upward to at most 6; three proxies is a 9-18/min budget.

limits.$comment: Flipkart's product limit lives in Settings; capacity here is not used for Flipkart.
